span.label: Cognitive load in undergraduates using AR for science learning, and how it relates to their self-efficacy and observed learning behaviour.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Do students split into distinct cognitive-load types rather than lying on one scale, and if so do those types differ in self-efficacy and in what they actually do?
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Four cognitive-load profiles - Low Engagement, Immersive, Dabbling, Organized - that differ measurably in self-efficacy and in behaviour sequences.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Collaborating and discussing with peers distributes the information-processing burden between students, which lowers each student's mental load and frees effort for performance
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The transaction costs of collaborating are themselves effortful, so heavy interaction can push cognitive processing into overload rather than relieving it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: cognitive load is treated as multi-dimensional, so a learner can be high on one dimension and low on another - which is why a single scale hides the types
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: extraneous load comes from how the material was designed rather than from its difficulty, so it is the component an instructor can remove
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: self-efficacy is proposed as the link between load and outcome: a sense of competence assists the cognitive processing itself
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AR adds load as well as benefit - multitasking between the virtual and real layers pulls attention off the instructions
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The profiles rest on only three self-reported cognitive-load dimensions within AR-based activities
span.note: what this limits: the profiles as a description of cognitive load: they rest on AR-BASED LEARNING ACTIVITIES AND THREE TYPES OF COGNITIVE LOAD: MENTAL LOAD, MENTAL EFFORT, AND PERFORMANCE, all self-reported
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Objective process measures such as eye and hand movement tracking were not collected and are needed to characterise the visual and motor behaviour behind the cognitive load
span.note: what this limits: any process-level reading: OTHER MEASURES OF COGNITIVE PROCESSES, SUCH AS EYE AND HAND MOVEMENT TRACKING, MAY NEED TO BE CONSIDERED FOR FUTURE STUDY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The literature it builds on disagrees with itself about the sign of the effect - more load has been reported as better, worse and neutral.
span.note: what this limits: the prior literature this builds on, which reports every possible sign: MORE COGNITIVE LOAD MAY PERFORM BETTER (... THEES ET AL., 2020), LESS FAVORABLY (... THEES ET AL., 2020), OR WITH NO SI[gnificant difference] - the same source cited on both sides
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The three classical load types are stated to be an incomplete account, and the paper adopts a second framework alongside them rather than resolving the conflict.
span.note: what this limits: the three-type framework itself: it is stated to be an incomplete account, and a second framework is adopted alongside it
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: One cohort, one country, one task - 365 Chinese undergraduates in a single AR activity.
span.note: what this limits: the generality of the profiles: 365 CHINESE UNDERGRADUATES in a single AR activity

span.label: Latent profile analysis of three cognitive-load dimensions sorted the undergraduates into four profiles, named Low Engagement, Immersive, Dabbling and Organized.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The Immersive profile (100 students) combined the highest mental effort with the lowest mental load and the second-highest performance of the four profiles.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Immersive-profile students reported the highest science learning self-efficacy of any profile.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Low Engagement students scored lowest on every self-efficacy dimension measured.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Organized-profile students outscored Dabbling students specifically on conceptual understanding and higher-order cognitive skills.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Profiles whose behaviour sequences included discussing with peers, taking tests and reading feedback had significantly higher self-efficacy than profiles whose behaviour was mainly taking tests and visiting resources.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The four-profile solution was preferred because it had the lowest AIC and adjusted BIC once the five-profile model was ruled out for containing a group under 10% of participants.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Dabbling and Organized students differed significantly only on conceptual understanding and higher-order cognitive skills, not on the other four self-efficacy dimensions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The Organized profile achieved the highest performance of all four profiles while carrying high mental effort and only medium mental load, alongside more communicative and collaborative behaviour.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Organized and Dabbling students, though similar in mental load, differed behaviourally in that Organized students finished tasks progressively while Dabbling students re-browsed materials and retried tasks with new answers.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Learners fall into four cognitive-load types rather than varying along one dimension.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The profiles differ in self-efficacy, with Low Engagement lowest on every dimension and Immersive highest overall.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Organized learners outperformed Dabbling ones on conceptual understanding and higher-order skills.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: What students actually did differed by profile, and the sequences involving social interaction and reviewing feedback went with higher self-efficacy than test-and-browse sequences.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
